findings: The repository source preserves only a hand-written topological-sort request; Java, graph representation, vertex numbering, Kahn/BFS, ordering policy and cycle API are not recovered source constraints.
The candidate explicitly labels Java, 0..V-1 vertices, int[][] directed edges, arbitrary-valid-order semantics, Kahn processing and exception-on-cycle as answer-side choices.

The Kahn invariant and cycle argument are sound for the declared contract: only current zero-indegree vertices are emitted, outgoing edges are removed once per edge record, and an empty frontier with unprocessed vertices implies a directed cycle.

An independent permutation-existence oracle, using neither Kahn nor DFS cycle detection, validates every simple directed graph through four vertices: 4,166 graphs total, 573 DAGs accepted with valid orders and 3,593 cyclic graphs rejected.
Reviewer checks additionally validate 800 seeded DAGs up to 40 vertices, duplicate-edge bookkeeping, self/cyclic rejection, empty graph behavior and declared invalid-input boundaries.
No fixed-order assumption, fabricated project experience, unsupported source expansion or unresolved source variant was found.
